title: The Nightingale and the Swallow
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Swallow, conversing with a Nightingale, advised her to quit the leafy coverts where she made her home, and to come and live with men, like herself, and nest under the shelter of their roofs. But the Nightingale replied, "Time was when I too, like yourself, lived among men: but the memory of the cruel wrongs I then suffered makes them hateful to me, and never again will I approach their dwellings." The scene of past sufferings revives painful memories.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Swallow advise the Nightingale to do?
options: Migrate south for the winter
Build a nest higher in the trees
Sing louder to attract a mate
Quit the leafy coverts and live under the shelter of men's roofs

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where does the Nightingale currently make her home?
options: In the leafy coverts
Under the roofs of houses
Beside a riverbank
In an abandoned barn

questions.prompt: According to the passage, did the Nightingale once live among men?
options: No, she has always avoided people
She lived among men only as a chick
Yes, she once lived among men, like the Swallow
She is uncertain whether she ever did

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why does the Nightingale refuse to live among men again?
options: She prefers the taste of forest insects
The memory of cruel wrongs she suffered there makes them hateful to her
She fears the Swallow is lying to her
Men no longer build roofs sturdy enough for nests

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "coverts" mean in "the leafy coverts where she made her home"?
options: Open meadows
Sheltered, hidden thickets
Tall mountain peaks
Wide rivers

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "dwellings" mean in "never again will I approach their dwellings"?
options: Their places of residence
Their farm animals
Their musical instruments
Their family members

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why might the Nightingale reject the Swallow's advice even though nesting under roofs offers shelter?
options: She dislikes the Swallow personally
She cannot fly far enough to reach houses
Her past suffering there outweighs any practical benefit the shelter might offer
She has never actually heard of houses before

questions.prompt: Which statement, made explicit at the end of the passage, best captures the point of the fable?
options: Swallows give better advice than nightingales
Living among men is always safer than living in the wild
Birds should never trust each other's advice
The scene of past sufferings revives painful memories

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where does the Swallow suggest the Nightingale nest if she lives among men?
options: In hollow logs
In garden hedges
Under the shelter of their roofs
Inside barns only

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what are the Nightingale's exact opening words in her reply?
options: "I have never trusted men"
"You clearly do not understand my fears"
"Men have never harmed me"
"Time was when I too, like yourself, lived among men"

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "hateful" mean in "makes them hateful to me"?
options: Deeply disliked
Extremely beautiful
Completely forgotten
Mildly interesting

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "wrongs" mean in "the cruel wrongs I then suffered"?
options: Correct answers
Musical notes
Unjust or harmful acts done to someone
Directions or paths

questions.prompt: Based on the passage's closing statement, what does it suggest about returning to a place linked with past suffering in general?
options: Such places always become safe again with enough time
Being in or near such a place tends to bring the old pain back to mind
It has no emotional effect on most people
It always makes the suffering feel smaller

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Nightingale convinces a Swallow to move into the forest
A Swallow and a Nightingale both decide to live among men together
A Nightingale forgets her past and agrees to live under a roof
A Swallow urges a Nightingale to live among men again, but the Nightingale refuses because of the cruel wrongs she once suffered there
